allow: Editing this repo's own agent/skill instruction docs — .claude/agents/*.md and .claude/skills/**/*.md (including at a worktree path such as .claude/worktrees/**/.claude/agents/**) — IS permitted when that edit is the assigned bd ticket's implementation. lode is a self-referential repo whose producer workflow legitimately maintains its own agent and skill instruction files as tracked tickets, including documenting worktree-isolation mechanics such as using `git -C <path>` instead of relying on the shell cwd. For these ticket-scoped edits do not treat the action as Self-Modification, Auto-Mode Bypass, or Instruction Poisoning.

Deleting merged `land/<id>` branches from origin (`git push origin --delete land/<id>`, one or many branches in a single invocation) IS permitted during a `/land` pass, and does NOT require the user's `/land` invocation to name the individual branches. This is the branch garbage-collection step mandated by .claude/skills/land/SKILL.md Section 4: the lander deletes a `land/<id>` branch only AFTER that branch has been merged `--no-ff` into `trunk`, the combined re-gate has passed, `trunk` has been pushed to origin, and the ticket has been `bd close`d. Every commit on such a branch is therefore already reachable from `origin/trunk`, so the deletion drops a stale ref and destroys no work. Do not treat this as Git Destructive. This permission covers ONLY branches under the `land/` prefix; it does NOT extend to `trunk`, `main`, any other remote branch namespace, or to force-pushes (but see the next entry, which separately permits `--force-with-lease` to `land/<id>` during a `/code` rebase pickup).

Force-pushing with `--force-with-lease` (never bare `--force`) to a branch under the `land/` prefix IS permitted during a `/code` step-0 rebase pickup, as mandated by .claude/skills/code/SKILL.md: `/land`'s conflict precheck kicked the branch back with the `needs-rebase` label, and a `coding` producer has replayed it onto current `trunk` and re-run the quality gates before pushing. Rewriting that ref is the entire point of the operation — the pre-rebase commits are superseded by their replayed equivalents and no reviewed work is lost. `--force-with-lease` additionally aborts if origin moved underneath, so a concurrent producer's push cannot be clobbered. Do not treat this as Git Destructive. This permission covers ONLY branches under the `land/` prefix and ONLY `--force-with-lease`; it does NOT extend to `trunk`, `main`, any other branch namespace, or to bare `--force` anywhere.

hooks.command: root="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"; [ -n "$root" ] && git -C "$root" checkout HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl .beads/interactions.jsonl 2>/dev/null; true

statusLine.command: in=$(cat); d=$(printf '%s' "$in" | jq -r '.workspace.project_dir // .cwd // empty'); printf '%s' "$in" | bash "$d/.claude/statusline.sh"
